questions.stem: A student places a plant cell and an animal cell in pure water. The plant cell does not burst but the animal cell does. What explains this difference?

options.text: Plant cells have a stronger cell membrane
Plant cells have a rigid cell wall that prevents over-expansion
Animal cells absorb water faster than plant cells
Plant cells do not take in water by osmosis

questions.explanation: The cellulose cell wall in plant cells is strong and rigid, preventing the cell from bursting (lysis) when water enters by osmosis. Animal cells lack a cell wall, so they swell and can burst in a hypotonic solution.

questions.stem: Root hair cells do not contain chloroplasts. Why is this appropriate for their function?

options.text: Roots are underground and receive no light for photosynthesis
Chloroplasts would block the absorption of minerals
Root cells are too small to contain chloroplasts

questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll for photosynthesis, which requires light. Since roots are underground where there is no light, having chloroplasts would serve no useful purpose. Root cells obtain glucose from the phloem instead.

questions.stem: A cell is found to contain a large permanent vacuole filled with cell sap, a cell wall, but no chloroplasts. Where in a plant would this cell most likely be found?

options.text: Either B or C could be correct

questions.explanation: All plant cells have a cell wall and vacuole, but not all have chloroplasts. Both root cells and petal cells lack chloroplasts -- root cells because they receive no light, and petals because their function is attracting pollinators rather than photosynthesis.

questions.stem: When making a microscope slide of onion epidermal cells, iodine stain is used. What does the iodine stain allow you to see more clearly?
questions.explanation: Iodine solution stains the nucleus a darker colour, making it visible, and also highlights the cell walls. Onion epidermal cells are transparent, so without staining, the internal structures would be very difficult to see under a light microscope.

questions.stem: A scientist discovers a single-celled organism with a nucleus, cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large vacuole. Which kingdom does it most likely belong to?
questions.explanation: The presence of a nucleus, cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large vacuole are characteristic plant cell features. Since it is single-celled, it could be a plant-like protist (such as a unicellular alga) or a very simple plant organism. It cannot be an animal cell (no cell wall/chloroplasts), bacterial (no nucleus), or fungal (no chloroplasts).
